question: If cluster-scale halos in published Lenstool posteriors mark where baryon-generated gravity appears to arrive, which observed baryonic structures are the least-distance launch points, and does their angular layout matter beyond their radial distribution?
claim_status: descriptive inverse reconstruction; it cannot establish that gravity followed the inferred paths or that the Lenstool halo locations are model-independent observations

field_interpretation.source_rule: Only baryons launch the candidate response; the posterior halo maps are arrival-location targets, not material sources in this interpretation.
field_interpretation.amplitude_rule: q is left unidentified. Every source and destination is normalized, so this stage tests geometry only.
field_interpretation.arc_family: Gamma_ij(t)=((1-t)x_i+t*y_j,4*h_ij*t*(1-t)); projected data constrain x_i and y_j but not the off-plane height h_ij.

halo_target.coordinate_rule: Lenstool posterior x is west-positive; convert to the project's east-positive registered frame with x_east=-x_Lenstool. Posterior y and project y are both north-positive. This was verified because the frozen MACS0329 second-halo initialization (36.7307733,17.0150976) arcsec maps to member 719 at project coordinates (-36.7306572,17.0150976) arcsec.
halo_target.component_rule: Include only posterior objects with x, y, core radius, and velocity dispersion columns; exclude external shear and member-galaxy potfile terms.
halo_target.support_gate: Every retained posterior halo center must lie inside the common 1200 kpc target aperture. The initial 650 kpc diagnostic support was rejected because it clipped the broad MACS1931 second-halo posterior.
halo_target.component_weight: posterior mean of sigma^2; sensitivity target gives every cluster-scale halo equal integrated weight
halo_target.interpretation_limit: The Gaussian occupancy kernels represent posterior halo locations and extents for backtracking. They are deliberately not claimed to be exact Lenstool dPIE convergence maps.

baryonic_sources.xray_limit: Soft X-ray event-rate morphology is an emissivity proxy, not a gas-mass measurement. Equal F160W/X-ray mixing is a sensitivity analysis, not a physical mass fraction.

controls.shuffle_rule: Preserve every member galaxy radius and light weight about the fixed origin while randomizing its polar angle; keep the halo posterior target fixed.
controls.primary_statistic: unregularized RMS projected transport distance from the regularized plan
controls.interpretation: A shorter real route than the shuffled routes means the observed member angles align with the assumed halo arrivals beyond radial concentration alone.

limits: Lenstool halo posteriors were inferred from the same strong-lensing observations and under the standard lens equation; this is circular if used as proof of a new field law.
Optimal transport selects the least projected-distance coupling and is not a unique physical trajectory.
The 2-D data cannot determine an arc height, travel time, causal propagation law, or stress-energy conservation law.
Normalized maps cannot identify the absolute response strength q.
F160W light has mass-to-light and membership uncertainty, while X-ray brightness is not gas mass.
All five clusters are spent exploratory systems. Any law derived here must be frozen and tested on new raw lens observables.
numerical_amendments: The first diagnostic output was rejected before interpretation because Lenstool west-positive x coordinates had not yet been converted to the registered east-positive frame.

The coordinate-corrected 650 kpc diagnostic output was rejected because it clipped the broad MACS1931 second-halo posterior; the final common support is 1200 kpc and must contain every retained halo center.
Difficult entropic-transport cases are retried at 2000 and then 10000 iterations; no solution outside the frozen marginal gates is saved.
